roughness parameters derived from medium-frequency roughness scales are the most suitable for the parameterization of the backscattering of agricultural soils.
the roughness scale that most affects the radar backscattered signal in agricultural soils is the medium-frequency rough scale (5–100 cm).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the medium-frequency rough scale is more important than the high-frequency rough scale and the low-frequency rough scale.
radar backscattering in agricultural soils seems to be mainly controlled by medium-frequency roughness.
radar measurements of agricultural surfaces are more sensitive to the medium-frequency rough components than to either the large- or small-frequency roughness components.
The main takeaway from our work is that
roughness measurements in the range of 5 to 100 cm should be considered in the future to accurately model the radar backscattered signal in agricultural soils.
radar measurements are more sensitive to medium-frequency roughness than to small- or large-scale components.
